title: Fork register
description: P4's deliverable (SPEC.md §4): one entry per interpretation fork, naming the ambiguous source text it interprets, every reading considered, which reading was taken and why. Under R4 (ANSWERED 2026-08-02, R4-FORK-REPRESENTATION.md) a fork that is materialised in L4 maps 1:1 to a field of the corpus's Interpretation record, and its readings map 1:1 to that field's enum constructors. Not every register entry is materialised: the BNA smoke test (PR #195) produced twelve ambiguities of which zero needed a runtime fork, so 'materialisation' is a discriminator and 'interpretation_field' is required only on the arm that has one. Paths under 'site' are validated for shape only — a register may be written before the file it points into is committed.

subject.description: The subject sidecar id under etc/go/subjects/, so a register cannot float free of the body of law it registers.

interpretation_type.description: The L4 record type the materialised entries are fields of; conventionally 'Interpretation'.

kind.description: 'authority' is a court or regulator whose word settles; 'scholarship' supports an argument without settling it. Keeping them apart is what stops a persuasive paper from reading as a resolution.

id.description: On a materialised fork this is the L4 enum constructor name, so the register and the encoding share one vocabulary.

status.description: 'rejected' = the encoder argued it away; 'demoted' = an authority struck it (R4 §1: a court striking a reading demotes, never deletes). 'arguable' = NEITHER: not taken, and not refuted — a reading the operative text forecloses, which a court could yet adopt. It exists because 'rejected' was carrying two different facts under one name, and only one of them is 'do not cite this'. A reader sizing exposure wants exactly the arguable list: readings live as law but not live in the encoding. ADDED 2026-08-09 ON ONE MEASURED INSTANCE, disclosed here rather than implied: F-100A1-CAP-vs-STATUTE's `statuteCap`, where Congress wrote $1,000,000 into 15 U.S.C. 77d(a)(6)(A) — the very paragraph the exemption is granted by, never since amended — and the Commission set $5,000,000 by rule. Nobody argued the statute away; the entry's own rationale says whether § 28's general exemptive authority reaches a specific numeric cap Congress placed in that paragraph 'is a question for a court, and no encoding settles it'. The other six entries in that register have genuinely refuted alternatives, so one instance is what this value rests on. If a second does not appear in the BNA's twelve dispositions or the charities corpus, reconsider it rather than let it become the bin every awkward reading is filed in.

foreclosure.description: For an 'arguable' reading only: what makes it non-operative, given that no one refuted it. Kept apart from `rejection_rationale` because the field names must not lie — nothing was rejected.

kind.description: What sort of ambiguity this is. The BNA's twelve rows forced all four: nine turn on the words (A1, A2, A4-A8, A10, A11); one is a vague undefined term with no competing parse (A3, 'new-born infant'); one is a counting convention the text does not rule on at all (A9); and one is not about the source words at all (A12, whether s 41A's good-character restriction narrows the s 1 entitlement or only the grant) — an ambiguity of encoding placement, which a wording-only schema would have had nowhere to put.

materialisation.description: How the fork lives in the encoding. 'interpretation-field' is R4's shape: a field of the Interpretation record, readings as its enum constructors, both readings executable. 'resolved-at-encode': one reading was taken on argument and the alternative is recorded but not encoded (all of the BNA's ten such rows). 'delegated-to-fact': the ambiguity is pushed into an input field whose construction the fact-supplier certifies (BNA A3, A9). Only the first arm is a fork the machinery can execute; the other two are a fork the register remembers.

interpretation_field.description: R4's 1:1 map: the Interpretation record field this entry is. Backticked L4 names are written without their backticks.

delegated_field.description: The input field that carries the construction, so a reviewer can find who bears the burden.

anchor.description: The L4 definition or § section the fork sits at. Not a line number, which rots on the next edit.

provisions.description: An array, not a string: BNA A1 ('after commencement') is one ambiguity spanning four subsections.

quote_absent_reason.description: Required when there is no quote. BNA A12 needs this: the restriction it is about sits in s 41A, whose text the ingest never fetched verbatim, so quoting it would have been invention.

citations.description: The same citation objects `readings[].citations` carries — an array, not a string, and not a string-or-array union. Two things measured 2026-08-09 forced it. (1) Three of the four entries in jl4/examples/legal/regcf/fork-register.json already held a citation OBJECT where this field declared `string`, so that register failed its own schema and nobody knew, because nothing had ever run the validator over it. (2) Twelve of the twenty-six entries in jl4/examples/legal/regcf/denovo/fork-register.json packed two or more distinct texts into one string, joined by 'read against', 'against' or a semicolon — which buries the very thing the entry exists to record: F-100A1-CAP-vs-STATUTE's source read '17 CFR 227.100(a)(1), read against 15 U.S.C. 77d(a)(6)(A)', a regulation set against the statute it is made under, and no query could see the second half or its `instrument` kind. One shape only, and no string alternative: `oneOf` is outside the keyword set etc/go/lib/register-validate.mjs implements, and a keyword parsed but not enforced is a constraint that silently does not exist.

readings.description: A fork with one reading is not a fork.

mechanism.description: How the choice is expressed. 'TYPICALLY' is the R4 default on the Interpretation field — the slot a settling authority gets cited at. The other two exist because a resolved-at-encode or delegated fork has no TYPICALLY to carry the citation, and pretending otherwise would put an authority's name on a construct that is not there.

status.description: STATUS IS ABOUT WHAT THE ENCODER DID, NOT ABOUT HOW MANY READINGS SURVIVE. 'open': the encoder took no reading — there is no `taken`, and the fork is disclosed unresolved. 'resolved': the encoder took one reading on its own argument — the BNA's twelve are all this, and a three-value open/settled/demoted vocabulary had nowhere to put them without either overclaiming an authority or leaving twelve entries permanently 'open'. 'settled': an authority settled it. 'demoted': an authority struck a reading. RULED 2026-08-09, because the earlier gloss defined 'open' by a live-reading count ('more than one reading is live and no authority has spoken') while defining 'resolved' by the encoder's act, and the two tests disagree: F-501A4-DETERMINER is 'resolved' with two readings still live, and F-100A1-CAP-vs-STATUTE was 'open' with one. Live-reading count is NOT the test — a reading may stay live because no authority has struck it while the encoder has nonetheless taken another. Crucially 'resolved' does not assert the underlying legal question is settled; that is exactly what 'settled' is for, and an entry may be 'resolved' while its `taken.rationale` records that a court could hold otherwise.

external_modification.description: The external-modifications register entry id that carries this authority, when the P2 sweep is what found it.

divergence.description: Whether the readings actually produce different answers — R4 §4's agreement/divergence split, and the field P6's witnesses hang off. 'none' is BNA A11's case: the readings differ in what they say but the encoding cannot tell them apart, because the field arrives pre-construed. 'unassessed' is honest at P4 time and is what forbids a report from claiming interpretation-independence it never measured.

witnesses.description: Named test cases that exhibit the divergence (R4 §4's divergence witnesses).

cross_refs.description: External-modifications register entry ids bearing on this fork. Empty is a normal answer and must be written out, so 'nobody looked' and 'nothing bears on it' are not the same JSON.

x-rules.description: No two entries share an id.
Reading ids are unique within their entry; on a materialised fork they are enum constructors, where a duplicate would not compile.
taken.reading names a reading of this entry whose status is 'live'. Taking a reading you rejected is the failure this catches.
Some reading must be live: a fork where every reading is rejected states no law.

materialisation 'interpretation-field' requires interpretation_field and forbids delegated_field; 'delegated-to-fact' requires delegated_field and forbids interpretation_field; 'resolved-at-encode' forbids both.
interpretation-field ⇒ taken.mechanism TYPICALLY; resolved-at-encode ⇒ encoded; delegated-to-fact ⇒ fact-supplied.
R4's 1:1 map: two entries may not claim the same Interpretation field.

A rejected or demoted reading carries a rejection_rationale. Every BNA row already wrote one; the schema makes it non-optional. 'arguable' is exempt and carries `foreclosure` instead — see the next rule.
A live reading carries at least one citation — R4 §1: each per-reading implementation carries @ref citations to the text that licenses its reading.

An 'arguable' reading is held to a HIGHER bar than a rejected one, not a lower one: it must cite the text that makes it arguable (it is, after all, law someone could win on) AND state in `foreclosure` what makes it non-operative, and it must NOT carry a rejection_rationale, because nothing rejected it. `foreclosure` is forbidden on every other status. The strictness is deliberate: the failure mode of a new enum value is that it becomes the bin for anything awkward, and a value that costs two fields to use does not attract lazy filing.
status settled or demoted ⇔ settled_by present.
status 'demoted' means an authority struck a reading, so some reading must have status 'demoted'.
Exactly one of source.quote and source.quote_absent_reason.
A materialised fork declares a divergence value (possibly 'unassessed'), because P6 owes it witnesses or an explicit agreement claim.
divergence 'observable' requires at least one witness: the claim that readings disagree is only as good as the case that shows it.
Witnesses without divergence 'observable' means the classification and the evidence disagree.
A register with no entries carries a note saying why — 'we found no ambiguity' and 'nobody ran P4' must not be the same file.
Every cross_refs id and every settled_by.external_modification names an entry of the external-modifications register.
All files given in one invocation name the same subject.
